newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexicans vote in key state election in Morelos.
newsitem.headline: Mexicans vote in key state election in Morelos.

text.p: Voters in the central state of Morelos trooped to the polls on Sunday to elect mayors and a state legislature in a key test of the strength of President Ernesto Zedillo's party.
The vote was seen as an early referendum on the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) ahead of widespread elections in various states in July.
Despite fears of violence in the state just south of Mexico's capital city, the elections in Morelos took place calmly and without any reported major incidents.
"Everything is quiet and is going well. We have installed 100 percent of the voting boxes," the president of the state Electoral Institute, Teodoro Lavin Leon, told Reuters.
With 860,000 registered voters, Morelos is one of Mexico's smaller states but its proximity to Mexico City gives it a high political profile.
Voters will elect 33 mayors, including in the capital Cuernavaca, and 30 deputies for the local Congress.
Voters gave Zedillo's PRI a tough time in the polls in 1995 and 1996, punishing it for the country's dire economic crisis and numerous corruption scandals.
PRI officials hope economic recovery and a more vigorous campaigning style will turn the tide against the opposition.
Polls suggested the vote in three of biggest municipalities was likely to be very close.
The PRI state governor, Jorge Carrillo Olea, has recently been in the headlines after the New York Times reported he had links to drugs traffickers. He denied the charges.
Carrillo's government has also suffered from citizen protests against a wave of kidnappings in the state.

Once home to peasant leader Emiliano Zapata, who led a revolt during the 1910-17 Mexican Revolution, Morelos is now better known as the state that press reports said contained two homes of wanted drug lord, Amado Carrillo Fuentes.
